title: Public Sector edition evidence reconciliation

method.verificationRule: verified means the cited URL was fetched or an official search result exposed the mapped proposition; partial means only a narrower proposition was checked; unverified means no bounded source established the proposition.
method.urlRule: Only URLs actually fetched or returned by bounded web search are present. A source without a URL is retained as a draft blocker rather than assigned a placeholder.
method.lineRule: lineSpan points to the supplied attachment or to the shared application paragraph in that attachment.

sources.label: GOV.UK Chat: five things learned from testing
sources.supports: The GDS evaluation reports an 18-month test, two public pilots, more than 10,000 users, 26,000 questions, a latest reported accuracy figure and bounded guardrail testing.
sources.limitation: Self-reported service-owner evaluation; the measures do not establish readiness for transactions or universal public-sector performance.

sources.label: Evaluating Consult: an AI tool for public consultation analysis
sources.publisher: UK Government AI.gov.uk and Scottish Government evaluation
sources.supports: The evaluation reports bounded theme-analysis results, including exact theme match, F1, reviewer agreement and review-time measures, with limitations.
sources.limitation: One live consultation and a specific tool/version; it is not evidence that the tool replaces accountable review.

sources.label: Proactive family benefits, Estonia (shared application evidence)
sources.publisher: Estonian Social Insurance Board via OECD Observatory of Public Sector Innovation
sources.supports: The case study describes a proactive family-benefit offer after a registered birth and reports that 97 percent of parents previously applied.
sources.limitation: Self-submitted case record; it does not establish the supplied processing-time or satisfaction figures, and it does not support the separate planning-document digitisation example.

sources.label: Zero Government Bureaucracy Phase 2 launch and Phase 1 results
sources.supports: Phase 2 launch of the Zero Government Bureaucracy programme and its service-simplification purpose.
sources.limitation: The WAM page returned a fetch error in this pass; the exact 4,000-plus, 1,600, 70-percent and 690-team figures were not line-checked.

sources.label: UAE to move 50% of government services to AI within two years
sources.supports: The April 2026 announcement of a two-year framework to deploy agentic AI across 50 percent of UAE government sectors, services and operations.
sources.limitation: The statement is a policy commitment; it does not establish delivery, accuracy or realised benefit.

sources.label: Abu Dhabi Digital Strategy 2025–2027
sources.supports: AED 13 billion programme, AI-powered government ambition, sovereign-cloud target and more than 200 AI solutions.
sources.limitation: GDP and jobs figures are sponsor projections, not measured outcomes.

sources.label: World Economic Forum recognition of UAE PASS
sources.supports: The UAE PASS recognition and a reported total exceeding 12 million registered users.
sources.limitation: Registration is not coverage; the checked result did not establish the supplied 15,000-service and 350-entity figures.

sources.label: TAMM 3.0 launch and service scope
sources.supports: TAMM 3.0 as an AI-powered one-stop platform and its reported service scope.
sources.limitation: The checked result reported more than 800 services, not the supplied 1,150; it did not publish accuracy or containment metrics for the citizen assistant.

sources.label: UAE data protection law overview
sources.supports: Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021 and the official UAE government's overview of its data-protection scope.
sources.limitation: The exact government-data/government-authority exclusion and executive-regulation status require the decree-law and current regulations, not only the overview page.

sources.label: Digital Government Authority establishment and mandate
sources.supports: DGA establishment by Cabinet decision on 9 March 2021 and its role as the national reference for digital government.
sources.limitation: The source establishes the authority and mandate, not every maturity or service statistic in the copy.

sources.label: Digital Experience Maturity Index 2026 results
sources.supports: 87.06 percent overall, 59 platforms, more than 805,500 participants and 76.98 percent digital inclusion in the 2026 index.
sources.limitation: Self-assessment by the issuing authority; assessed platform count changed year on year, so movement is not like-for-like.

sources.label: Nafath adoption figures
sources.supports: SDAIA's official open-data material identifies Nafath statistics as a published dataset.
sources.limitation: The checked source did not establish the supplied 3-billion, 23.5-million and 530-plus bundle with one reporting period and denominator.

sources.label: Absher service and transaction figures
sources.supports: Absher processed 33,644,074 transactions across Individuals and Business during March 2025.
sources.limitation: The checked SPA report does not establish the supplied 460-service and 28-million-digital-identity figures.

sources.label: UN E-Government Survey 2024
sources.supports: Saudi Arabia ranked sixth in the 2024 UN E-Government Development Index with an EGDI value of 0.96022.
sources.limitation: The supplied source row's regional-ranking wording should be checked against the report narrative separately.

sources.label: Personal Data Protection Law and Implementing Regulations
sources.publisher: Royal Decree M/19 as amended; SDAIA
sources.supports: The PDPL defines public entities as controllers and provides the legal framework for processing and transfers; SDAIA publishes implementing materials.
sources.limitation: Registration, transfer, cloud and breach propositions must each be cited to the current law, implementing regulation and relevant controls.

sources.label: BALSAM Arabic benchmark
sources.publisher: SDAIA and King Salman Global Academy
sources.supports: BALSAM is an Arabic LLM benchmark with 78 tasks across 14 categories and a large test/development corpus.
sources.limitation: The checked paper does not establish the supplied 22-model, 12,786-question and 0.88-convergence figures; it reports a different benchmark structure.

sources.label: Türkiye AI Action Plan 2026–2030
sources.supports: The Ministry page identifies the Türkiye Artificial Intelligence Action Plan 2026–2030.
sources.limitation: The fetched page exposed a PDF loading shell; the four axes, 16 actions and governance text were not checked line by line.

sources.label: Presidential Decree 183 of 28 March 2025
sources.supports: The supplied copy attributes consolidation of public-sector digital transformation and public AI applications to this decree.
sources.limitation: The dated official Gazette issue page was found, but its decree text was not exposed by the bounded fetch; the decree number and proposition still require issue-level legal-text confirmation.

sources.label: e-Devlet Kapısı service statistics
sources.supports: The official gateway is a single access point for personal information, documents and services from public institutions.
sources.limitation: The fetched landing page did not establish the supplied 69.5-million users, 9,396 services and 1,128 institutions as at 31 August 2026.

sources.label: MERNİS and KPS
sources.publisher: Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü
sources.supports: The official NVI MERNİS page identifies the population-register system and its institutional context.
sources.limitation: The supplied 2000/2002 dates and 20-days-to-55-seconds processing claim were not line-checked on the fetched page.

sources.label: Integrated Social Assistance System
sources.supports: The ministry/World Bank case study describes Turkey's integrated social-assistance system, including data integration and electronic eligibility/payment workflows.
sources.limitation: The fetched study describes 22 institutions and 112 web services; it does not establish the supplied 52-query, 16-institution, 30-million-citizen and 340-million-transaction bundle.

sources.label: UN E-Government Survey 2024
sources.supports: The UN country page reports Türkiye at rank 27 with a 2024 EGDI of 0.8913.
sources.limitation: The supplied 76.1-percent citizen-use figure was not established by the checked country page.

sources.label: TR-MMLU and TurkishMMLU
sources.supports: TR-MMLU is a natively written Turkish benchmark with 6,200 multiple-choice questions across 62 sections; TurkishMMLU is a separate Turkish benchmark with more than 10,000 questions.
sources.limitation: The supplied copy's broader public-sector conclusions require the cited benchmark papers and should not be generalized beyond their test designs.

sources.label: Decision (EU) 2022/2481 — Digital Decade Policy Programme
sources.supports: The Digital Decade 2030 targets for public services, health records and electronic identification.
sources.limitation: Targets are policy objectives and do not establish realised delivery.

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 — Single Digital Gateway
sources.supports: The Single Digital Gateway regulation and once-only technical-system framework, including the Annex II procedure context.
sources.limitation: The regulation is not evidence that every supplied implementation statistic has been realised.

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 — European Digital Identity
sources.supports: The European Digital Identity Framework and its wallet obligations.
sources.limitation: The exact 24 December 2026 deadline should be quoted from the implementing-act entry-into-force calculation, not inferred from a summary.

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — Digital Omnibus on AI
sources.supports: The amended AI Act dates, including Article 113's 2 December 2027 Annex III and 2 August 2028 Annex I dates and Article 111's distinct legacy public-authority step to 2 August 2030.
sources.limitation: The supplied line 102 compresses several distinct obligations; the consolidated act and relevant amendment provisions must be cited separately.

sources.label: eGovernment Benchmark 2025 and 2026
sources.supports: The Commission benchmark methodology covering key public services and life events.
sources.limitation: The checked Commission page did not establish the supplied 93-percent Single Digital Gateway figure or its denominator.

sources.label: Proactive family benefits, Estonia
sources.publisher: OECD Observatory of Public Sector Innovation
sources.supports: A self-submitted case describing proactive family-benefit offers after registered births and reporting that 97 percent of parents had previously applied.
sources.limitation: The fetched case study did not establish the supplied 9.8 out of 10, two-hour-to-thirty-second figures; it is a delivering-institution case record.

sources.label: EU20 multilingual benchmark suite
sources.supports: Academic work studying quality assurance for the EU20 multilingual benchmark suite.
sources.limitation: The checked publication describes a 20-language translated suite; it does not establish the supplied 21-language performance-gap figures.

unresolved: Shared application mappings: all 12 rows now link bounded GOV.UK Chat, Consult or Estonia OPSI URLs and carry explicit institutions and jurisdictions. The separate planning-service document-digitisation example remains unresolved because its institution and source were not located.
UAE: exact Phase 1 Zero Government Bureaucracy results, UAE PASS connected-service/entity totals and TAMM 1,150-service figure require source-level reconciliation.
UAE: Federal Decree-Law 45 government-data exclusion and executive-regulation status require the decree-law/current regulations.
Saudi Arabia: Nafath 3bn/23.5m/530-plus bundle and Absher 460-service/28m-identity figures need dated primary datasets.
Saudi Arabia: BALSAM supplied 22-model/12,786-question/0.88 figures do not match the checked benchmark paper.

Türkiye: the Presidential Decree 183 row now links the dated 28 March 2025 Resmî Gazete issue page, but the page text was not exposed by the bounded fetch; decree-number and proposition confirmation remain an explicit legal-text blocker.
Türkiye: e-Devlet, MERNİS/KPS and BSYS supplied metric bundles need their named official reports; the checked BSYS source is a 2017 case study with different counts.
EU: the exact 24 December 2026 EUDI deadline, 93-percent Single Digital Gateway statistic and 21-language EU20 performance figures need their exact table/article sources.
EU: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 dates must not be compressed into one date; cite the separate Article 111 and Article 113 obligations.

The shared critical-perspective lines 78-80 and line 92 contain NYC/TIGTA/containment assertions, but the supplied section-8 tables do not include those source rows; preserve as editorial review blockers rather than inventing source rows.
